headline: Inferring connectivity and dynamics from simulated neurons and single-cell expression
label: Inferring Dynamical And Causal Models
summary: Recent preprints and a published method test whether inferred dynamical and causal models recover hidden structure and predict gene-expression trajectories.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inferring structured dynamical or causal models from observed activity and evaluating them against ground truth, identifiability, or predictive performance. A graph neural network decomposes simulated neural assembly dynamics to jointly recover connectivity, neuron types, and signaling functions. DynML applies multiplexed Lorenz and Rossler reservoir computing to gene-expression dynamics in liver regeneration and Drosophila embryogenesis, reporting that topological entropy correlates with predictive power. STICCC separates reversible from irreversible single-cell state transitions using gene expression and regulatory networks. HORDCOIN, a software library, reduces connected information estimation under entropic constraints to a linear program. What is new is the pairing of dynamical complexity measures with directional transition inference at single-cell resolution.
